title: I'm 22 and earn RM4,000. Should I buy my first property now?
videoTitle: ASKING SEAN #252 | NOT TOO YOUNG, BUT TOO EARLY
excerpt: A 22-year-old engineer wants a RM460,000 new launch near Damansara with zero down payment. Sean tells him to wait a few years and build the basics first.

qa.asker: EY, a viewer who wrote in by email
qa.context: EY is a 22-year-old engineer at a multinational in Penang, earning about RM4,000 a month before tax and EPF, with little savings and a clean CCRIS record. He has surveyed many projects from PJ to KL and likes a freehold three-bedroom new launch near Damansara at about RM460,000 after rebates, with zero down payment and completion expected in late 2027.
qa.question: Should he buy it now as his first property, given his belief that it isn't a good time to invest?
qa.quote: If I will be 22 again I will not buy property just yet.
qa.answer: Not yet. At 22, a 35-year commitment of about RM2,250 a month on a take-home pay of about RM3,000 will dictate his career and life choices. He should spend three to five years building his career, insurance, emergency fund and savings, then buy with more options.

reasons.title: The basics come first
reasons.body: Before any property: medical and personal accident cover, about six months of expenses as an emergency fund, and clarity that this career is the one. At 22 he may yet change field, move overseas or marry, and the instalment would tie his hands.

reasons.title: Property keeps you rich
reasons.body: Sean treats property as a way to diversify wealth, not to make money. A RM500,000 loan at 4% over 35 years costs about RM945,000 in total, so you only gain if the property grows faster than the cost of financing.

reasons.title: Savings unlock better deals
reasons.body: With no savings he can only buy new launches. With about 18% of the price saved, roughly RM90,000 for a RM500,000 unit, he can buy a completed subsale nearby, see exactly what he gets, rent it out within six months and declare the rent for his next loan.

reasons.title: Check who the advice comes from
reasons.body: His view that the market is past its best came from someone else. Sean says to listen only to people with skin in the game; over 20 years Malaysian property has appreciated about 4% a year, and his own portfolio's rents have risen 22% to 23%.

actions: Get basic medical and personal accident cover, without overpaying.
Save six months of expenses as an emergency fund you don't touch.
Aim to save about 18% of your target price over the next three to four years.
Wait until your take-home pay is about RM5,000 and you are sure of your career, then buy.
If you still like the project when it completes, buy a subsale unit then, or a cheaper subsale of about RM300,000 whose rent covers the instalment.
qa.caveat: Sean thinks the project itself is reasonably priced; his objection is the buyer's timing and affordability. He also says he knows the developer and has reviewed its earlier projects.

sourceNote: Summarised from Sean's full English captions for Asking Sean #252, sponsored by PropertyGuru's Brickz transaction reports. The quoted answer is verbatim; everything else is paraphrased. Figures are as Sean stated them in June 2024.
